title: Sleep and Weight: Understanding the Connection

authorship.current_visible_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team
authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: How does sleep quality and duration affect weight, appetite hormones, and metabolism?
reader_intent: Understand the mechanisms connecting sleep to hunger hormones, food choices, and metabolic health.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader understands ghrelin/leptin/cortisol responses to sleep loss and the approximate magnitude of insulin-sensitivity impact, and adopts practical sleep-hygiene steps.

claims.proposition: Just a few nights of restricted sleep can reduce insulin sensitivity by 25-30 percent.
claims.recommended_action: A specific, checkable statistic with zero citation. This figure is consistent with published short-term sleep-restriction studies (e.g., Donga et al. 2010-type single-night sleep restriction research) but was not independently reverified against a primary source this audit — verify the exact figure and population before restating with this precision.

internal_link_recommendations.reason: Near-identical reader job; should be consulted together until merged.

disposition_reason: More substantive and mechanistically detailed than its near-duplicate (how-sleep-affects-weight-health-daily-functioning) and selected as the cluster survivor, but it has zero citations anywhere and one specific, unverified statistic (25-30% insulin sensitivity reduction) that needs a primary-source check before this article can be considered adequately sourced.
required_research: Verify the exact insulin-sensitivity reduction figure and study population against a primary sleep-restriction study.
recommended_rewrite_scope: Verify or requalify the specific insulin-sensitivity statistic.
Fold in the merged article's practical, plain-language framing where it adds value.
